title: Judges 17
paragraphs: ¹ There was a man named Micah from the hill country of Ephraim. ² He said to his mother, "The eleven hundred pieces of silver that were taken from you — I heard you utter a curse about it. Look, I have the silver. I took it." His mother replied, "The LORD bless you, my son!" ³ When he returned the eleven hundred pieces of silver to his mother, she said, "I solemnly dedicate this silver to the LORD for my son, to make an idol overlaid with silver. So now I will give it back to you." ⁴ He returned the money to his mother, and she took two hundred pieces of silver and gave them to a silversmith, who made them into an idol. It was placed in Micah's house. ⁵ Now this man Micah had a shrine, and he made an ephod and some household idols and consecrated one of his sons to be his priest.

⁶ In those days there was no king in Israel, and everyone did whatever seemed right to them. ⁷ There was a young man from Bethlehem in Judah, from the tribe of Judah, who was a Levite living there. ⁸ He left Bethlehem to find a place to settle and came to the hill country of Ephraim, stopping at the house of Micah along the way. ⁹ Micah asked him, "Where are you from?" He answered, "I'm a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I'm looking for a place to live." ¹⁰ Micah said to him, "Stay with me and be my priest and spiritual father — I'll pay you ten pieces of silver a year, provide your clothing, and give you your meals." The Levite agreed to stay.

¹¹ The Levite was happy to live with the man, and Micah treated the young man like one of his own sons. ¹² Micah installed the Levite as his priest, and the young man lived in Micah's house. ¹³ Micah said, "Now I know the LORD will be good to me, because I have a Levite as my priest."
